{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-9098.25","title":"radio.py: enter_rx during in-flight TX hears overlapping frames","description":"## Problem

`_do_start_transmission` documents half-duplex: starting TX aborts this node's RX window (timeout, callbacks, stash) without deleting TxEnd / TxStartDelayed. The reverse is missing.

`enter_rx_mode` and `start_receive` set `NodeState.RX_WAIT` even when `_active_transmissions[node_id]` is set and the medium still holds that TX. They do not `end_tx`, and `_get_rx_result_internal` never checks TX / `_active_transmissions`. Live `get_rx_candidates` still resolve.

`test_deliver_pending_preserves_tx_end` (9098.22) does exactly this — `start_transmission("rx")`, `start_transmission("tx")`, `advance_to(1000)`, `enter_rx_mode("rx")`, `deliver_pending_packets()` — and only asserts TxEndEvent survives. It does not assert `received` is empty. "rx" can hear "hello" while its own airtime is still running.

HIL (`node_server` / `renode_server` / `serial_server`) maps firmware RX_ENTER to `enter_rx_mode`. A RX_ENTER before TxDone (or a turnaround race) lets the sim deliver overlapping foreign packets that an SX126x cannot hear with the PA on. Protocol tests pass in sim and fail on hardware.

`NODE_STATE_TRANSITIONS` allows TX→RX_WAIT, so the state machine will not catch this.

This is not 9098.22 (RX teardown deleting TxEnd/TxStartDelayed). 22 kept the TX lifecycle events. This is the RX path treating an in-flight transmitter as a receiver.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py (`enter_rx_mode`, `start_receive`, `_get_rx_result_internal`; no active-TX guard)
- python/tests/sim/test_radio.py (`test_deliver_pending_preserves_tx_end`)
- python/src/lichen/sim/node_server.py / renode_server.py / serial_server.py (RX_ENTER)

## Why this is robustness

Half-duplex is a hard radio constraint. TX already tears down RX; RX must not hear while this node's TX is on the medium.
